speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash, specifically whether it is flat or raised, and where exactly on your body it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash have a "slapped cheek" appearance, and is the rash on her extremities lacy or reticular in pattern? I also need to know if she has any joint pain or if anyone else in her household has had similar symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities is classic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
